title: SLO-aware proactive draining and fractional hedging routing policy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a production-ready routing policy that minimizes SLO violations during regional capacity pressure and partial outages by combining (1) proactive draining of at-risk hosts, (2) fractional hedging across nearby regions for tail-latency protection, and (3) capacity-aware geo-pinning with graceful shedding. This ticket describes the design, rollout plan, experiments, and observability hooks.

Background: We observe that short-lived capacity spikes and slowdowns in a region cause cascading latency SLO violations as the regional allocator continues to send requests until saturation triggers hard circuit breakers. Existing steering policies are reactive (detect capacity loss then redirect) which still yields tail spikes. We need a policy that (a) reduces amplification of spikes, (b) preserves locality for latency-sensitive customers, and (c) gracefully sheds low-priority traffic before saturating regional slots.

Core ideas: 
- SLO-driven scoring: compute a per-route score using moving-window P95 and P99 latency trends, regional capacity headroom, and token-concurrency quota utilization. Score is scaled so routing decisions directly target reduction in projected SLO breach probability.
- Proactive draining: when a host/instance's score crosses a soft threshold (based on SLO velocity), gradually drain new requests (percent-based) while allowing inflight completions. Draining windows are fractional (e.g., drain 25% of new requests immediately, 50% within next 30s) so we avoid abrupt failovers.
- Fractional hedging: instead of all-or-nothing hedging, send a small percentage (fraction f) of replicas of particularly long-running requests to a secondary region chosen by latency/cost tradeoff. f is adaptive: increases when projected SLO violation risk grows. Hedged replicas are cancelled on first response. This reduces p99 tail risk without large capacity tax.
- Capacity-aware geo-pinning: maintain a pin score per customer/route that prefers a home region but allows spillover when headroom is healthy. Pin score factors: observed cross-region latency delta, customer tier, SLO sensitivity, and remaining capacity credits. Pins degrade gracefully under sustained pressure (soft to hard unpin thresholds).
- Circuit breaker hierarchy & shedding: introduce a two-level circuit breaker: a soft CB that triggers progressive draining and fractional hedging, and a hard CB that rejects or throttles based on configured priority classes. Low-priority traffic is shed first; retries are routed to cheaper fallback models/regions where applicable.

Observability & experiment plan: 
- Dashboard with model per-route score, per-region headroom, p95/p99 forecast, drained fraction over time, hedged replica ratio, and CB events. Link: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/routing/eng-91877 
- Synthetic benchmark: load tests across three regions with staged CPU/GPU saturation to measure SLO leakage reduction vs baseline (current steering).
- Canary rollout: feature flag with three gates: metrics-only -> canary (10% traffic) -> ramp (50% -> 100%). Canary region selection: eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1.

Trade-offs and open questions: 
- Cost: hedging increases total token work. We mitigate by keeping f small and only enabling hedging during elevated risk windows. Need finance sign-off on cost thresholds.
- Complexity: new scoring function and two-tier CB increases control plane state. Plan to reuse existing regional metrics stores and add a compact TTL cache for scores to avoid high-cardinality sprawl.
- Backpressure interactions: draining must signal to autoscaler and admission controller to avoid fighting autoscaling policies; coordination API needed.

Artifacts: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/ENG-91877+Proactive+Draining+and+Fractional+Hedging
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/compare/feature/proactive-drain-91877
- Load-test script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/routing-hedging

Success criteria (high-level): measurable reduction in P99 breaches for latency-sensitive routes under staged regional degradation with <15% incremental token cost during typical conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring engine computes per-route per-region risk score every 5s with <150ms median processing latency
Proactive draining increments are applied per-host and honoured by router without dropped in-flight requests
Fractional hedging reduces p99 tail by at least 30% in synthetic regional slowdowns for targeted routes
Two-tier circuit breakers trigger soft draining then hard rejects according to policy and are configurable per-customer tier
Canary rollout metrics-only phase produces no more than 0.5% change in baseline cost and no customer-facing errors

Implement hedging client logic with adaptive fraction and cancellation on first response
Add pin score store and expose pin override APIs for Console

Create load-test harness and run staged degradation scenarios
Prepare canary rollout runbook and alert thresholds
